author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: The Philippines and France signed an agreement that facilitates mutual military visits as Manila seeks partners in countering Beijing’s expansive claims over the South China Sea.
title: France, Philippines Sign Military Agreement Amid China Tensions

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said he would sign an order to pay Transportation Security Administration officers in a bid to alleviate disruptions at US airports with lawmakers in Congress deadlocked on how to end a partial government shutdown.
title: Trump Says He Will Sign Order to Pay TSA Agents During Shutdown

author: Daniel Flatley
description: Donald Trump’s signature will appear on future US paper currency to mark the 250th anniversary of the country, a first for a sitting president, according to the Treasury department.
title: Trump’s Signature to Appear on US Currency, Breaking Precedent

description: Congressman Gabe Amo, a Democrat from Rhode Island, calls on Republicans to come to the table with a “good faith” deal to end the homeland security shutdown amid ongoing negotiations. He also discusses the financial toll of the Iran conflict, including higher gas prices for his constituents. Rep. Amo speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Amo Urges 'Good Faith' DHS Deal, Slams ‘Chaos’

author: Jeff Mason, Joe Lovinger
description: The biggest annual political conference for American conservatives, normally a spotlight for unity around President Donald Trump and his policies, is showing cracks of dissension as the war in Iran nears its fifth week.
title: MAGA Divide Over Iran Spills Into CPAC, Where Some Blame Israel

description: Senator Pete Ricketts, a Republican from Nebraska, says he's prepared to remain in Washington to secure a homeland security funding agreement as negotiations drag on ahead of a scheduled recess. He also discusses developments in the Iran conflict and his Stop Insider Trading Act. He speaks with Joe Mathieu outside Capitol Hill on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Ricketts Urges DHS Deal, Signals Willingness to Stay In Town to Negotiate

author: Manolo Serapio Jr, Haslinda Amin
description: Four years after Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. won a landslide victory alongside now arch-rival Sara Duterte, the landscape looks a lot different. Their alliance that propelled him to power lies in ruins and he’s grappling with an energy crisis triggered by the Iran war plus fresh political strain from a widening corruption scandal over flood-control spending.
title: Philippines’ Marcos Airs Fears Former Ally Could Undo His Legacy

description: Michael Zezas, deputy global head of research and co-director of the Morgan Stanley Institute, joined the program to provide insights during a period of heightened market volatility. The discussion took place against the backdrop of breaking news that the pause on Iran energy strikes has been extended, a development influencing crude oil prices. Michael Zezas spoke with Katie Greifeld and Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Extends Energy-Attack Ceasefire: Morgan Stanley's Zezas Reacts

author: Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: A bipartisan group of senators introduced legislation Thursday that would require lawmakers and government employees to disclose any bets they place through prediction markets in a bid to prevent public officials from profiting on privileged information.
title: Senate Bill Seeks to Curb Insider Bets on Prediction Markets

description: Traditional allies see the US under Donald Trump as an unreliable partner. Now they’re looking to hedge their bets by way of China, just as Xi Jinping positions his nation as the “adult in the room.”  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Making China Great Again?

author: Sarah Holder, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: On today’s Big Take podcast, why Netflix bowed out of the bidding for Warner Bros. Discovery, the regulatory hurdles that remain for Paramount and how these two big movie studios will become one.
title: Anatomy of a Deal: Inside the Epic Bidding War for Warner Bros.

author: Nancy Cook
description: Party leaders are taking a more-the-merrier approach on political styles
title: For Midterm Candidates, Democrats Go With All of the Above

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss the latest on US and Iran's back and forth as skepticism over a potential ceasefire grows, sending stocks lower. Bloomberg News White House and National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko and Ann Miletti, Head of Equity Investments at Allspring Global Investments, both weigh in. Then, Tannenbaum Capital Group Founder Len Tannenbaum joins to discuss the latest in private credit as $5 billion worth of investor capital remains trapped behind withdrawal limits. Plus, Alicia Chong Rodriguez, Founder and CEO of Bloomer Tech, joins to discuss the company's smart bra that helps women track biometric data to aid in heart disease detection and treatment. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stock Selloff Gains Speed on Ceasefire Doubts | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/26/2026

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Republican Senator Ted Budd, Democratic Congresswoman Suzan DelBene, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Rebelle Communications CEO Laura Fink and Retired Rear Admiral John Kirby. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Questions Iran Deal | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/26/2026

description: A group of bipartisan Senators want to make sure lawmakers can't use insider information and benefit by betting on prediction markets. Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin and and Republican Senator Todd Young spoke first with Bloomberg's David Gura and Christina Ruffini about the legislation they helped introduce.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Senators Try to Put Guardrails Around Prediction Markets

author: Anna J Kaiser
description: La Administración Federal de Aviación prohibió todos los vuelos sobre Mar-a-Lago por debajo de los 2.000 pies, incluso cuando el presidente no se encuentre allí.
title: Trump logra restringir vuelos sobre Mar-a-Lago y desata protestas por ruido en Florida

description:
Washington Democratic Representative Suzan DelBene said that Americans' anger about broken promises from the Trump administration is powering support for Democrats ahead of midterm elections as voters look for candidates who aren't going to be a 'rubber stamp' for Donald Trump. DelBene, who serves as chair of the DCCC, said that Democrats have 44 districts in play and are on 'offense' against Republican challengers. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrats on 'Offense' in 44 Midterm Districts, Says DelBene

description: On today’s Big Take podcast, legal reporter David Voreacos takes Sarah Holder inside the federal investigation of Jeffrey Epstein two decades ago, and the mounting frustrations of the prosecutor who ran it. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Prosecutor Who Fought to Indict Epstein

author: Olesia Safronova, Volodymyr Verbianyi, Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy kicked off a surprise visit to the Gulf region as he seeks to offer his nation’s anti-drone expertise in exchange for defense support.
title: Zelenskiy Kicks Off Surprise Gulf States Tour With Defense Pitch

author: Courtney Subramanian, Edward Ludlow
description: White House adviser David Sacks said Congress could pass bipartisan artificial intelligence legislation within months, a move that would fulfill President Donald Trump’s pledge to create a national playbook for regulating the emerging technology.
title: Congress Could Pass AI Standard in ‘Months,’ Key Trump Aide Says

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: The Trump administration is investigating policies at three medical schools for “possible race discrimination,” according to a New York Times report. The Civil Rights Division of the US Justice Department is requesting data from Stanford University, The Ohio State University, and the University of California, San Diego.
title: US Probes Stanford’s Medical School Over Admission Policy, Report Says

author: Nicola M White
description: A pair of senators pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority about trading around the time of the US military action in Venezuela ousting President Nicolas Maduro.
title: Warren Presses SEC on Venezuela Bond Trades Before Maduro Ouster

description: Are social media like giants like Meta and Google facing a Big Tobacco moment? Nicole Sy explains how a landmark lawsuit over addiction threatens Big Tech. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Is Big Tech Facing Its Big Tobacco Moment?

author: Maggie Eastland, Oma Seddiq
description: A House panel advanced legislation that would require the Commerce Department to demand chipmakers do more to keep AI technology from being smuggled to China, an effort that’s gained new urgency after last week’s indictment of a Super Micro Computer Inc. co-founder for allegedly diverting Nvidia Corp. processors to Chinese buyers.
title: Chip Security Bill Advances in House Following Super Micro Case

author: Antonia Mufarech, Carolina Gonzalez
description: Chile’s truckers so far seem willing to accept steep increases in fuel prices if the new conservative government that many of them support delivers on its security pledge.
title: Chile’s Truckers Stick by Kast as Fuel Price Hikes Sow Tensions

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US President Donald Trump sent conflicting signals on the prospect that talks with Iran would bring a halt to the nearly month-long war, further roiling global energy markets.
title: Trump Questions If Iran Deal Possible, Roiling Energy Markets

author: Erik Wasson, Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Republicans have sent Democrats a revised proposal to end the ongoing shutdown at the Department of Homeland Security, which has snarled airport security lines around the country and added pressure on the US economy.
title: Republican Senators Make ‘Final Offer’ to End DHS Shutdown

description: European Commission Vice President Kaja Kallas speaks to Bloomberg's Oliver Crook about finding a way to end the wars in Iran and Ukraine, fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz and making sure Ukraine has the help it needs to fight Russia. They speak in France ahead of the G-7 meeting. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: EU's Kallas on War in Iran, Ukraine, Fully Reopening Strait of Hormuz

author: Lucy White
description: Reform UK’s deputy leader said big technology companies must “share the pain” with banks of reimbursing the victims of financial fraud facilitated by their platforms.
title: Reform UK Says Big Tech Must Share ‘Pain’ of Fraud With Banks

author: Zoe Tillman
description: It’s been a year since the Trump administration abruptly terminated the US legal status of thousands of foreign students, only to reinstate them weeks later amid a wave of lawsuits.
title: DOJ Struggles to Convince Judges to End Foreign Student Lawsuits

description:
Even as US President Donald Trump threatens to absorb Canada, some Alberta voters are determined to break it apart.

A long-simmering secession drive in the oil-rich province appears poised to reach the ballot this year, asking residents whether to stick with the rest of Canada or strike out on their own. Thomas Seal reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Alberta's Bid to Secede From Canada Poised to Hit October Ballot

description: President Donald Trump appointed tech industry leaders including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a new presidential technology council that will focus on artificial intelligence policy and other science-related issues. David Sacks, Craft Ventures partner and co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, joins Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Stacked Tech Council With ‘Star Power,’ David Sacks Says

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Skylar Woodhouse
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a US insurance program meant to boost shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will begin soon, a move that may help revive flows of much of the world’s oil and gas supplies.
title: Bessent Says Insurance Program for Hormuz Ships to Start Soon

author: Paige Smith, Emily Mason
description: Visa Inc., Mastercard Inc., PayPal Holdings Inc. and Stripe Inc. received letters from a Washington antitrust regulator warning the firms not to deny customers access to services based on their political or religious views.
title: Visa, Payment Firms Warned by Regulator on ‘Debanking’ Consumers

author: Roxana Tiron
description: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) said Thursday she’s working on a possible authorization for the use of military force in Iran as frustration rises in the president’s party with lack of detail over operations in the Middle East.
title: Murkowski, Key Swing Vote, Is Shopping Authorization on Iran War

description: President Donald Trump criticizes Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the Fed building renovation costs during a Cabinet meeting at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Jokes Warsh as Fed Chair Might Work at White House

author: Myles Miller
description: The Trump administration has expanded the role of Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers at some US airports, moving them from largely a support role into parts of the passenger screening process as staffing shortages strain the Transportation Security Administration.
title: ICE Agents Start Screening Travelers as TSA Staffing Issues Grow

description: President Donald Trump says he’s disappointed NATO did not cooperate with military operations in Iran. He speaks during a Cabinet meeting.
title: Trump Says ‘We’re Very Disappointed With NATO’

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: US President Donald Trump said NATO’s refusal to cooperate with US military operations in Iran was a “test” for the security alliance and that he would “remember” their response, ratcheting up his criticism of the bloc.
title: Trump Assails NATO, Says US Will ‘Remember’ Response on Iran

author: Brian Platt
description: Canada hiked its military spending enough in 2025 to reach the target set by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, fulfilling a promise made by Prime Minister Mark Carney shortly after winning an election last April.
title: Canada Spends 2% of GDP on Defense For First Time in Decades

author: Iain Marlow
description: The US warned that Iran-backed Houthi militants could start firing on vessels in the Bab El-Mandeb Strait after Tehran raised the possibility of extending barriers to global shipping during the ongoing war.
title: US Warns on Bab El-Mandeb Strait After Iranian Shipping Threat

author: Michelle Kaske
description: New York City’s doormen and building workers are set to hold a strike vote on April 15 as their union and an advisory board to property owners have yet to reach agreement on a new labor contract.
title: New York City Doormen, Building Workers Set April 15 Strike Vote

author: Foster Wong
description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged the international community to facilitate a return to negotiations over the war in Iran, saying China and Canada could play a “constructive role” in pursuing a political solution.
title: China’s Wang Reiterates Push for Iran Talks in Call With Canada

description: "They are begging to make a deal, not me," President Donald Trump says when asked about the progress of a possible diplomatic agreement with Iran during a Cabinet meeting at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He's Unsure About Brokering Deal With Iran

description: Speaking at a Cabinet meeting in the White House, President Donald Trump says he might have to take "drastic measures" to end the lengthy shutdown at the Department of Homeland Security. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He May Take Drastic Measures to End Shutdown

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungary’s election campaign took a darker turn in its final stretch with the government and opposition trading accusations of foreign espionage and manipulating law enforcement, just as Prime Minister Viktor Orban fights the biggest challenge to his 16-year rule.
title: Spying Charges Rock Hungarian Election Campaign in Final Stretch

author: Simon Casey
description: The chairman of the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said big tech companies seeking more power for their data centers don’t engage enough with her agency.
title: US Regulator Chides Big Tech for Lack of Engagement on Grids

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said he’s unsure about reaching a diplomatic agreement with Iran, another signal the two sides remain at loggerheads about efforts to end the nearly month-long war.
title: Trump Expresses Uncertainty About Brokering Deal With Iran

author: Chris Strohm
description: The Federal Reserve asked a judge to stand firm in his decision to dismiss two Justice Department subpoenas seeking information about building-renovation cost overruns tied to the administration’s legal fight with Chair Jerome Powell.
title: Federal Reserve Urges Judge to Be Firm on Quashing DOJ Subpoena

description:
President Donald Trump is telling Iran it "better get serious" about negotiations, but Becca Wasser, defense lead for Bloomberg Economics says any talks are likely "doa." She speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest.  
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Negotiations With Iran Are Likely 'DOA,' Says Wasser

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark’s caretaker Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen invited parties from across the political divide to initial talks on forming a ruling coalition.
title: Denmark’s Frederiksen Opens Cross-Bloc Talks to Form Government

author: Andrea Palasciano, Max Ramsay
description: Russian intelligence is helping Iran target Americans and US allies, according to the European Union’s foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas.
title: Russia Is Helping Iran ‘Kill Americans,’ EU’s Top Diplomat Says

author: John Gittelsohn, Alicia Clanton
description: Californians haven’t elected a Republican governor since Arnold Schwarzenegger in 2006. But in this year’s race, opinion polls are suggesting the unthinkable for Democrats: a potential two-man showdown in November in which both candidates are from the GOP.
title: In Deep-Blue California, Two Republicans Lead the Governor’s Race

author: Charlie Wells
description: The UK replaced the chief executive of the country’s state-backed savings bank, National Savings and Investments, as it grapples with a scandal over the mismanagement of customer money.
title: British Savings Bank NS&I Replaces CEO Amid Management Scandal

author: Dana Khraiche, Dan Williams
description: As it wages war on Iran in concert with the US, Israel is fighting on a second and more familiar front — against the Iran-backed militia Hezbollah in neighboring Lebanon. Hezbollah began lobbing mostly short-range rockets and drones into Israel the day after the operation against Iran began, the intensity of the salvos posing a threat to Israel on a par with Iran’s ballistic missiles. In response, the Israelis have carried out intensive air strikes on Lebanon and sent ground troops into the sout
title: Israel Versus Hezbollah: Why the Iran War Has Spread to Lebanon

author: Konrad Krasuski
description: Poland is joining a group of countries that shield consumers from surging fuel prices with a plan to cut taxes and cap prices at the pump, according to Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
title: Poland Plans Fuel Tax Cuts to Shield Consumers From High Prices

author: Michael Nienaber
description: Germany and Australia plan to improve space security through a joint network of sensors which will create a global early-warning system for satellite sabotage.
title: Germany, Australia Team Up On Space Security, Laser Weapons

author: Misha Savic
description: Montenegro is the “the most advanced country on the path” to joining the European Union but still needs to speed up reforms required for membership, according to the bloc’s top official for enlargement.
title: EU Enlargement Chief Says Montenegro in ‘Endgame’ of Accession

description: A recap of Bloomberg Invest New York, the flagship event in Bloomberg Live's 2026 series, featuring interviews with leaders in asset management, banking, private capital and wealth. Hosted by Dani Burger. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Best of Bloomberg Invest 2026

author: Anna J Kaiser, Michael Smith
description: President Donald Trump will be headlining a three-day conference this week in Miami Beach showcasing the power and wealth of Saudi Arabia, an annual bash that lures titans of finance and politics for a chance to tap into the Kingdom’s riches.
title: Trump to Headline Saudi Conference in Miami as Iran War Rages

author: Ethan Bronner
description: Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.
title: As World Seeks War’s End, Israelis Hold Out for Full Victory

author: S'thembile Cele
description: France withdrew an invitation for South Africa to attend a summit of Group of Seven leaders in June following pressure from the US, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s office said.
title: US Urged France to Revoke South Africa G-7 Invite, Pretoria Says

author: Bob Van Voris
description: Nicolás Maduro is set to return to a Manhattan federal court Thursday as the US pushes forward with a broad drug-trafficking and narco-terrorism conspiracy case against the ousted Venezuelan leader that’s loaded with regional and geopolitical implications.
title: Nicolás Maduro Back to Court as He Fights Narco-Terrorism Case

author: Ignacio Olivera Doll
description: Cracks emerging in Argentina’s economic growth are now threatening one of President Javier Milei’s signature achievements: the fiscal surplus.
title: Argentina’s Sluggish Economy Is Testing Milei’s Spending Cuts

author: Anuradha Raghu, Kok Leong Chan
description: Malaysia’s government will cut subsidized allocations for its most popular fuel from April as it seeks to curb leakages and relieve fiscal pressure from a surge in oil prices owing to the Middle East conflict.
title: Malaysia Cuts Subsidized Fuel Quotas on Global Oil Price Surge

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump pressed Senate Republicans to change the chamber’s rules in a way that would allow them to secure funding for the Department of Homeland Security without Democrats, invoking the long lines and delays at some airports amid the partial government shutdown.
title: Trump Urges Republicans to End Filibuster to Ease Airport Delays

author: Jenny Che, Oliver Crook
description: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said she will press at a meeting of Group of Seven foreign ministers for a reduction in hostilities in the US- and Israel-led war in Iran as countries around the world contend with a surge in energy prices.
title: Canada to Push for Deescalation in Middle East at G-7 Meeting

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark’s parliament is on the cusp of gender parity after female representation hit a record high in this week’s vote.
title: Women Win Record 48% of Danish Parliament Seats in Vote

author: Magan Crane
description: President Donald Trump threatened Iran with intensified military action, seeking to pressure the country to ramp up negotiations on an end to the war even amid uncertainty over the status of those discussions.
title: Trump Urges Iran to Negotiate a Deal Before It Is ‘Too Late’

author: Michal Kubala
description: Arms manufacturer CSG NV, owned by Czech billionaire Michal Strnad, said the conflict in the Middle East is creating fresh business opportunities as the company seeks to further expand into advanced defense technologies.
title: Defense Firm CSG Sees Iran War Boosting Demand for New Systems

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Top national Republican political groups are outraising Democrats 4-to-1
title: Democrat Fundraising Is Falling Short Ahead of Midterms

author: Gian Volpicelli
description: The European Union opened an investigation into Snap Inc.’s social network and escalated a probe into a number of pornography platforms as the bloc ramps up efforts to protect children online.
title: EU Targets Snapchat, Porn Websites in Child Protection Push

author: Andrea Palasciano, Slav Okov
description: NATO’s European allies and Canada increased their defense spending nearly 20% for the second straight year in 2025, yielding to US President Donald Trump’s demands and responding to mounting threats from Russia.
title: NATO Says Europe and Canada Spent 20% More on Defense in 2025

author: Flavia Krause-Jackson
description: Iranian theocracy’s resilience seems to come as a surprise to Trump.
title: Trump’s Frustration Grows With Implacable Iran

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: Ukraine said it targeted a key Russian export-oriented oil refinery in the Leningrad region overnight, as Kyiv has carried out intensive attacks on Baltic energy infrastructure this week.
title: Ukraine Says It Attacked Russia’s Major Baltic Refinery Kirishi

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: German officials see a risk that the nation’s economy will grow at just half the pace they had envisaged if the Iran war drags on, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Germany Sees Danger of 2026 Growth Rate Halving on Iran Crisis

author: Jorge Valero
description: European Union lawmakers finally approved a trade deal with the US, clearing a key obstacle for the long-delayed agreement despite lingering uncertainty about Washington’s tariffs.
title: EU Lawmakers Approve US Trade Deal After Several Delays

author: Petra Sorge
description: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said the coalition may introduce additional measures to help alleviate the impact of surging fuel prices after lawmakers approved an initial package.
title: Germany to Consider Additional Fuel Measures, Minister Says

description: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand says she held discussions on Monday with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the conflict in the Middle East. "I indicated that Canada wants to play a role in this diplomacy," Anand tells Bloomberg's Oliver Crook. They speak on the sidelines of the Group of Seven foreign ministers meeting in Vaux-de-Cernay, France. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Canada Wants a Role in US-Iran Diplomacy, Anand Says

author: Philip Aldrick
description: Britain will suffer a bigger economic hit from the Iran war than any other Group of Seven nation this year as growth weakens, inflation accelerates and interest-rate cuts are abandoned, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned.
title: UK Faces Worst Hit From War Among Major Economies, OECD Warns

description: Anna Rosenberg, head of geopolitics at Amundi Investment Institute, discusses the potential deployment of US troop in Iran. "If Trump decides to go big, then you're going to have a situation which is going to be very messy," Rosenberg tells Bloomberg Television. "But our base case is that he goes home, and doesn't go big." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump's Iran Options Constrained by Domestic Politics, Amundi Says

description: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven countries are meeting in Vaux-de-Cernay, France, to discuss the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: G-7 Foreign Ministers to Discuss Iran, Ukraine Conflicts

description: Justin Muzinich, CEO of Muzinich & Co., says investors are looking past short-term war noise, with the Gulf remaining an attractive destination for capital as his firm expands in Abu Dhabi. He spoke to Joumanna Bercetche on Horizons Middle East & Africa. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Muzinich: Gulf Investors Look Past Short-Term Noise

author: Catherine Lucey, Nancy Cook, Bill Allison
description: Democrats are barreling toward the midterm elections with advantages in messaging, polling and voter enthusiasm. But they’re falling short of their Republican rivals on one of the most important metrics of all: money.
title: Democrats’ Midterms Prospects Undercut by Donors Who Say 2024 Cash ‘Went Up in Smoke’

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is struggling to respond to Flavio Bolsonaro’s rise in polls as tensions mount within his inner circle over how to counter the surge, adding to a string of crises denting his approval and threatening his chances in the final electoral campaign of his career.
title: Lula Struggles to Blunt Bolsonaro’s Rise in Tight Brazil Race

author: Manuela Tobias
description: President Javier Milei’s approval rating fell in March to the lowest level since he took office as corruption allegations ensnared his government, unemployment climbed and Argentines soured on his trade deal with the Trump administration.
title: Milei’s Approval Rating Hits New Low as Argentina Unemployment Rises

author: Gonzalo Soto
description: President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval rating plunged to the lowest levels of her term in March, as Mexicans expressed deepening worries about corruption and crime following the killing of a notorious cartel leader.
title: Sheinbaum Approval Falls to Lowest of Presidency on Crime Fears

author: Arsalan Shahla, Kateryna Kadabashy, Eltaf Najafizada
description: Israel and Iran exchanged missile strikes as the status of potential peace talks remains uncertain, extending a war that’s wreaked havoc across the Middle East and global markets.
title: Israel and Iran Keep Up Strikes With Talks to End War Uncertain

description: Oil rose as the US and Iran offered conflicting comments on efforts to end the war that’s led to the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The global crude benchmark is on pace for the biggest monthly gain since 1990. Bloomberg's Anthony di Paola reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Climbs as US, Iran Argue Over Terms to End War

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark’s central bank warned the domestic economy could take a significant hit if the conflict in the Middle East drags on, urging caution on public spending as government negotiations get underway.
title: Danish Central Bank Flags Risks as Government Talks Get Underway

author: Julian Harris
description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer brushed off concerns that the theft of his former top aide’s phone was in any way linked to an investigation into the UK government’s appointment of Peter Mandelson as US ambassador.
title: Starmer Plays Down Mandelson-Epstein Theories Over Stolen Phone

description: Military strikes are continuing in the Middle East as US President Donald Trump’s Friday deadline for Iran to negotiate a deal to end the war approaches. Israel said it struck infrastructure in Isfahan, in the center of Iran, while the UAE and Bahrain reported Iranian missile and drone threats. Iran’s armed forces said they carried out missile strikes targeting American forces and separatist groups backed by the US-Israeli alliance in the northern Iraqi city of Erbil. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: No Letup in Military Strikes as Trump's Iran Deadline Approaches

author: Miaojung Lin, Yian Lee
description: Ko Wen-je, the former Taipei mayor who ran a high-profile, outsider campaign for president in 2024, was convicted of graft-related charges and sentenced to a total of 17 years in prison, the semi-official Central News Agency reported, citing a court ruling on Thursday.
title: Ex-Taiwan Presidential Candidate Ko Wen-je Jailed for 17 Years

description: As NATO scales up defense spending, Slovakia is turning into a critical ammunition powerhouse. Over the past four years, exports of defense products have risen 2,200% to €2.4 billion ($2.9 billion). Bloomberg's Daniel Hornak reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Slovakia Is Becoming an Ammunition Powerhouse as NATO Ups Spending

author: Kamil Kowalcze, Michael Nienaber, Jenny Leonard
description: The next time Donald Trump tries to push America’s traditional allies into line, the German government intends to be better prepared.
title: Germany Is Drafting Plan to Hit US Companies in Next Trump Clash

description: Smoke rises from Kuwait international airport after a drone strike on fuel storage in Kuwait City on March 25. AP Photo
title: Clash Over US-Iran Peace Talks Leaves War’s End Unclear

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: A Turkish tanker in the Black Sea laden with crude oil reported a suspected undersea attack early Thursday but there was no oil spill, maritime authorities said.
title: Oil Tanker in Black Sea Reports Undersea Attack, Turkey Says

author: Akemi Terukina, Yoshiaki Nohara
description: It is not acceptable for the US to unilaterally impose a peace plan upon Tehran, Iran’s ambassador to Japan Peiman Seadat said Thursday, as the two countries continue to wrangle over peace talks with no clear conclusion to the conflict in sight.
title: US Can’t Impose Unilateral Peace Plan, Iran Envoy to Japan Says

description: Zack Polanski is challenging the notion that you can’t be Green and a popular politician. Since he became the leader of the UK’s Green Party in September 2025, he has run a campaign that’s pushed his party ahead of the incumbent Labour Party and opposition Conservative Party in some polls. It’s a remarkable rise in a short span of time – how did he pull it off and what will he do if the Green Party gets into power? (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Polanski’s Plan to Tax Billionaires, Make Energy Cheap

author: Daniel Hornak, Andrea Dudik
description: Slovakia makes more autos than anywhere else in the world relative to its size. Now defense firm CSG is scaling up production of shells to become a key European supplier.
title: Europe’s Carmaking Powerhouse Wants to Become Its Ammunition Hub

author: Andrea Palasciano
description: Ukraine is struggling to secure fresh commitments from NATO allies to purchase US weapons for the war-torn country, Kyiv’s envoy to the military alliance said.
title: Ukraine Struggles to Find More NATO Donors to Pay for US Weapons

author: Heesu Lee
description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called on the public to pare back power usage and ride public transport rather than driving cars as his government mounts a national effort to avoid energy shortages should the Iran conflict drag on.
title: Korea’s Lee Urges Less Power Use, Driving to Avoid Energy Crunch

author: Augusta Saraiva, Shawn Donnan, Jade Khatib
description: Four in 10 US counties shrank last year as President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown continued to stifle the nation’s main source of population growth.
title: More US Counties See Population Drops Under Trump’s Immigration Crackdown

author: Jim Wyss
description: The retired US colonel behind a privately financed rocket launch site in the Dominican Republic sees the project as a response to China’s dominance of the space race in Latin America.
title: Dominican Republic Is Next Frontier in US-China Space Race

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon, Sakura Murakami
description: Japanese ground forces are set to actively participate in military exercises in the Philippines for the first time in post-World War II history next month, marking the deepening of ties between Manila and Tokyo’s armed services as both countries face strained relations with China.
title: Japan to Join Army Drills on Philippine Soil in First Since WWII

author: Colum Murphy, Charlie Zhu
description: China’s No. 3 official Zhao Leji called for the political settlement of international disputes, positioning Beijing as a stabilizing force as the continuing conflict in Iran threatens to upend the global economy.
title: China’s No. 3 Leader Urges Peaceful Solutions as Iran War Drags

author: Claire Jiao
description: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said China will be crucial in anchoring Asia’s growth prospects at a time when the global economy is strained by conflict and trade fragmentation.
title: Singapore Says China Can Play Bigger Role in Asia’s Stability

author: Mathieu Dion
description: Quebec’s powerful government pension manager criticized Air Canada for making a video statement only in English about the deadly collision at LaGuardia Airport, adding to the woes of Chief Executive Officer Michael Rousseau.
title: Quebec Pension Fund Caisse Condemns Air Canada CEO’s Video, Joining Carney

author: Yoshiaki Nohara, Akemi Terukina
description: Japan should consider sending warships to help jointly secure the Strait of Hormuz with other nations and protect both its own vessels and those of other nations — even before a ceasefire, according to a former top national security adviser.
title: Japan Should Send Warships to Secure Hormuz, Ex-Adviser Says

author: Jon Herskovitz
description: The UK will interdict and board Russian “shadow fleet” vessels in its waters, increasing European pressure on Moscow over tankers exporting sanctioned crude in transactions that help fund the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine.
title: Britain to Intercept Russian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Ships in UK Waters

author: Josh Wingrove
description: Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte has sent letters to the Department of Justice encouraging prosecutors to open new fraud investigations into New York Attorney General Letitia James related to real estate.
title: Pulte Makes New Fraud Allegations Against New York AG James

author: Catherine Lucey, Hadriana Lowenkron, Annmarie Hordern
description: President Donald Trump insisted Republicans have momentum in the upcoming midterm elections, even as the party faces a harsh electoral landscape and pressure from the White House over legislative priorities.
title: Trump Insists GOP Is the ‘Hot Party’ Despite Midterm Headwinds

author: Tom Rees
description: The threat of surging inflation has knocked UK consumer confidence to the lowest level recorded under Keir Starmer’s Labour government.
title: UK Household Confidence Plunges to Lowest Under Starmer
